correctness.rationale: All full-dimensional total-matching vertices are classified by k disjoint edges and at most one-side unmatched vertex support. The uniform saturated matching orbit has barycenter c and constant radius R2, giving a variance lower-bound certificate for all centers. For the stated inequality the exact distance maxima reduce to strictly monotone L_k and B_k, whose endpoint difference is [d(p-d)-2p]/q; this proves containment, uniqueness and every contact. Necessity follows from the convex hull of contacts and unique symmetry fixed point. A complete divisibility argument gives the three ties. Exact rational checker replayed successfully.

The closest indexed geometric results concern inscribed spheres, ordinary matchings, or other graph polytopes; their assumptions and claims do not imply this ambient outer-sphere result. value.rationale: For the canonical total-matching polytope, the theorem completely identifies a natural sharp one-orbit minimum-sphere phase with factorially many contacts, classifies all exceptional integral ties, and provides an exact radius and center. It explains a nontrivial screening of all other graph-vertex and partial-matching configurations; this is not a mere counting restatement or a routine renaming of the known facet description.
